claims.text: A $10M base with four options against a $22M total appropriation indicates roughly $12M was obligated across the option years, but no obligation-by-year record has been released and the contract does not appear in public USAspending data because DIA procurement is exempt from FPDS reporting under 10 USC 424.

Contract number HHM402-08-C-0072; contract signed 22 September 2008; awarded off solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211 (posted 18 Aug 2008, responses due 5 Sep 2008). Modification P00001 effective 02 September 2009 exercised/continued the effort.

DIA's own 16 December 2008 status briefing is headed 'Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Contract Status — Contract HHM402-08-C-0072' and describes the contract focus as 'Advanced (unconventional) aerospace weapon' technologies.

The contract does not appear in public federal contract data: an FPDS-NG ATOM query for PIID "HHM402-08-C-0072" returns an empty result feed, and USAspending.gov returns 404 for the corresponding generated award IDs.

Absence from FPDS/USAspending is expected for DIA Virginia Contracting Activity awards (intelligence-community contracting is generally excluded from public reporting), but it means the only public award record for a $22M program is the FOIA-released paper. Dollar-value line items on the modification are illegible/redacted in the released scan.

desc: This is the money. Contract HHM402-08-C-0072, awarded 22 September 2008 by the Defense Intelligence Agency to Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies, LLC of 4640 S. Eastern Avenue, Las Vegas NV 89119 (DUNS 827037768, CAGE 54JU7), firm fixed price, $10,000,000 base value, base period 22 September 2008 to 21 September 2009 with four one-year options. Line items cover monthly status reports, project management plans, research reports on advanced aerospace weapon systems, an integrated threat assessment, and travel and other direct costs. The contracting officer, COR and Government Project Leader are all redacted under 10 USC 424 in the released copy — the same Lacatski whose name DIA had printed in the public solicitation five weeks earlier. DIA withheld this contract entirely from a 2011 FOIA response and did not release it until 13 October 2022 under FOIA-00349-2018, a fourteen-year gap between award and disclosure of a contract that was competed on a public bid board. A September 2009 modification exercising the FY10 option was released separately.
